item.title: Microsoft says it "restored service" after major worldwide outage
item.description: A Microsoft outage involving services like Outlook and Teams impacted many users, companies and government services.

item.title: Alaska elects first Democrat governor since 1998
item.description: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, also known as JKT, campaigned on issues including affordability and funding of public schools

item.title: U.N. watchdog agency pushes for access to key Iran nuclear site
item.description: As Trump signals he may let the Iran war fester, the U.N. nuclear agency is "increasingly concerned" about access to a key uranium facility, according to a leaked report.

item.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights
item.description: The rare nationwide ground stop lasted about five hours Friday. Sources told CBS News an update to the network connecting the air traffic control system caused a reboot, crash and outage.

item.title: Passengers rescued after tanker hit river cruise in New Orleans
item.description: A tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans Friday, partially submerging the passenger boat.

item.title: How "Banana Man" took a small Indiana town by storm
item.description: Banana Man began popping up around Linton, Indiana, a few months ago. Videos that also began circulating on social media appeared to show a boy biking all over town in a banana suit.

item.title: Nationwide ground stop lifted, Duffy calls for congressional funding to upgrade ATC system
item.description: The FAA on Friday night lifted a nationwide ground stop issued hours earlier over what DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called a telecommunications outage. Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy took questions on the situation from the White House.

item.title: SpaceX launches first-of-its-kind Starship test flight
item.description: The SpaceX Super Heavy-Starship was designed from the ground up to be fully reusable in a bid to lower launch costs.

item.title: Lutnick agrees to testify as Bessent blames him for chip sales
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Man whose wife, son were injured in building collapse wants answers
item.description: The world crumbled around Anderson Velez's family on Wednesday when the multi-use Brooklyn building where they resided collapsed.

item.title: Small Indiana town gets its own superhero, a kid known as "Banana Man"
item.description: A boy became a local legend in Linton, Indiana, for regularly riding his bike in a banana costume, earning him the nickname "Banana Man." Steve Hartman has the story.

item.title: SpaceX launches huge Starship rocket on 15th test flight
item.description: SpaceX launched its massive Starship rocket on its 15th test flight on Friday, but it was unsuccessful in controlling the booster's landing. The company has successfully caught the rocket's booster three times before. Jason Allen has the story.

item.title: Bessent upset Lutnick didn't ban Nvidia chip exports to China-linked firm
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is blaming Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for allowing Megaspeed, the firm once led by alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, to circumvent U.S. restrictions by funneling Nvidia chips to China, CBS News has learned. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing and China denies the spying allegations. Ed O'Keefe has the story.

item.title: West Coast braces for storm system that could unleash 50-foot waves
item.description: The West Coast is bracing for severe weather over the weekend after the East Coast saw tornadoes this week. Rob Marciano has more.

item.title: Father whose wife and sons were inside Brooklyn building during collapse shares his story
item.description: Anderson Velez, who lived in the Brooklyn building that collapsed on Wednesday while his wife and two children were inside, tells Lilia Luciano what he thought when he saw video of the moment the building came down.

item.title: No fatalities after tanker hits river cruise ship in New Orleans, officials say
item.description: Authorities said at least 32 people were treated at local hospitals after a tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the port of New Orleans. All passengers have been accounted for. Skyler Henry has more.

item.title: Latest developments on FAA's national ground stop
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a national ground stop on Friday, with officials citing "extraordinary circumstances" and safety concerns. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Former FAA chief spokesperson says ATC system is "horribly outdated" amid ground stop
item.description: Former FAA chief spokesperson Scott Brenner joins CBS News to discuss Friday's nationwide ground stop and the age of America's air traffic control system. Then, Lindsay Gutierrez, a passenger stranded at JFK Airport, joins to share her experience.

item.title: Democrats strategize on how to deliver on midterm mandate
item.description: Democrats gathered in Denver this week for a conference on what comes next as they prepare to take control of Congress.

item.title: Stranded passenger in Las Vegas on nationwide ground stop: "Nobody has answers"
item.description: Clara Pablo was trying to get home from Las Vegas to New York on Friday when the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop. She joined CBS News' to share her experience. Then, CBS Atlanta's Nakell Williams reports on the scene from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

item.title: Travelers facing uncertainty amid nationwide ground stop
item.description: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop Friday, snarling travel plans for people across the country. CBS News' Carter Evans and Caitlin Huey-Burns have more.

item.title: All accounted for after tanker hits river cruise ship in New Orleans, 32 hospitalized
item.description: All are accounted for and 32 people have been hospitalized after a tanker hit a river cruise ship in New Orleans. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Update to network connecting ATC system led to outage before ground stop, sources say
item.description: An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News. Lindsey Reiser anchors continuing coverage.

item.title: 11/13: CBS Evening News
item.description: Latest on FAA's national ground stop; No fatalities in New Orleans ship collision.

item.title: 11/13: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: The FAA issues a nationwide ground stop, with DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin saying it's due to a telecommunications outage.

item.title: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeats Lauren Boebert in House race
item.description: Colorado Democrat Eileen Laubacher has defeated incumbent Republican Congresswoman Lauren Boebert to represent the 4th Congressional District, CBS News projects.

item.title: Family Dollar to pay $63M after FTC says it overcharged customers
item.description: The discount retailer failed to honor prices displayed on store shelves, on price tags and in ads, the FTC and multiple states alleged.

item.title: Inflation isn't going away. Here's what that means for interest rates.
item.description: As inflation seeps deeper into the U.S. economy, the Federal Reserve may have to step up the pace of rate hikes, according to Wall Street analysts.

item.title: World Food Programme director on Gaza's worsening food crisis
item.description: Nearly a million displaced people are enduring flooding and food shortages in Gaza. This comes amid a devastating food crisis. Ross Smith, the director of emergencies for the World Food Programme, comments on the deteriorating conditions.

item.title: GOP lawmakers press Huang and Lutnick to testify over Nvidia
item.description: Republicans on Capitol Hill are negotiating for now-resigned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang​ to appear before Congress.
